posts.title: Alberta votes Oct. 19: what's on the ballot

slides.headline: Alberta votes Oct. 19. Here's what's on the ballot.
details: Advisory|The government isn't bound by the result
slides.footer: Sources: Alberta referendum question · Abacus Data · LiveWire Calgary

slides.headline: Word for word:
details: “Should Alberta remain a province of Canada or should the Government of Alberta commence the legal process required under the Canadian Constitution to hold a binding provincial referendum on whether or not Alberta should separate from Canada?”
Council voted Sept. 22 to call Calgary “a vital part of Alberta and Canada.”
Only Ward 12 Coun. Mike Jamieson voted no. The vote is symbolic: it doesn't change the ballot.

slides.headline: Nothing separates on Oct. 19.
details: If the second option wins, the province is asked to start the legal process toward a later, binding referendum on separating.
Voting day is Monday, Oct. 19. Save this.

posts.caption:
ALBERTA VOTES OCT. 19 🗳️ Swipe for what's actually on the ballot.

The separation question is one of 10 on the ballot. Picking the second option doesn't separate Alberta. It asks the province to start the legal process toward a later, binding vote. And the result doesn't bind the government either way.

Latest poll (Abacus Data, Sept. 4–7): 64% remain, 24% hold a separation referendum.

Calgary's council went on record Sept. 22, voting 14–1 to call Calgary "a vital part of Alberta and Canada."

Save this for Oct. 19.

Sources: Government of Alberta referendum question, Abacus Data, LiveWire Calgary, CTV News.

posts.title: Calgary rents are down from a year ago

slides.headline: Calgary rents are down from a year ago
slides.footer: Source: Zumper Calgary rent report, September 2026

posts.caption:
RENT IS FALLING IN CALGARY 📉

Median 1-bed: $1,590 (down 10% from last year)
Median 2-bed: $1,890 (down 11%)
Calgary overall: $1,800 a month, about $100 under the national median.

Our take: if your lease is up soon, this is a year to negotiate. Bring these numbers.

Source: Zumper Calgary rent report, Sept. 2026.

posts.title: Our take: show us the bill for new suburbs

slides.headline: Every new suburb should come with its bill printed on it.
details: $28M|Property tax a year, once fully built

posts.caption:
OUR TAKE 🧾 Calgary keeps weighing new communities on its edge. We think every one should come with the bill up front.

Take Providence in the southwest: about 9,600 homes, $582.7 million in city-built infrastructure over several budgets, and about $28 million a year in property tax once it's fully built. More applications were headed to council this year.

Maybe that's a good deal. But Calgarians should see the math before it's approved, not after.

Worth it? Tell us in the comments.

This post is opinion. Figures: The Sprawl, March 21, 2026.
